Adrenal steroid biosynthesis disorder causing cortisol deficiency; electrolyte disturbances remain within the endocrine/metabolic axis.

Benign ovarian stromal tumour without endocrine dysfunction. Pleural effusion belongs to associated Meigs syndrome; Gorlin-associated skin/jaw findings are not intrinsic to ovarian fibroma.

Acquired porphyrin metabolism disorder, predominantly sporadic PCT; blistering skin injury is common (>30%). Associated hepatitis and other liver diseases are separate conditions.

A joint disorder defines the primary axis despite its transient course; an immune mechanism is not established for the umbrella.
Limb/body-wall defects and CNS malformations are defining features; renal and cardiac malformations each occur in 30-79%. Intestinal and hepatic abnormalities are occasional.
Perineurial nerve-sheath tumour usually arising in dermis or subcutis; rare visceral locations do not justify additional axes.
Benign NK-cell lymphoproliferation directly occupies gastrointestinal mucosa; it is not lymphoma, and no infectious or autoimmune mechanism is established.
Congenital fusion of proximal finger joints with associated skeletal abnormalities; hearing involvement is not established for this subtype.
Splenoportal venous malformations with hepatic fibrosis/cirrhosis characterize the disorder. Encephalopathy and diabetes lack frequencies; splenomegaly alone does not establish blood-organ damage.
